prompt: Aggregate a pile of crash reports into a blame summary showing which class shows up in the most stack traces. Complete CrashBlameAggregator, then run the tests.
explanation: The rule "one trace is one vote" is what the per-trace Set enforces: recursion or a retry loop can put OrderService in a trace four times, but the Set collapses those to a single increment so a deep recursion cannot dominate the summary. Peeling the name needs two lastIndexOf calls -- the first strips the method, the second strips the package -- because indexOf would stop inside the package. Because the counts live in a TreeMap, keys arrive alphabetically, so mostBlamed's strictly-greater-than comparison keeps the first (alphabetically smallest) name on a tie, and report only has to re-sort by count descending with the name as the tie-break.
hints: Inside addTrace, collect this trace's simple names into a Set first, then increment the long-lived Map once per distinct name.
Getting from "com.shop.order.OrderService.total(...)" to "OrderService" takes two lastIndexOf('.') steps: drop the method, then drop the package.
Use > (not >=) when scanning for the highest count over alphabetically ordered keys, and Comparator.comparingInt(...).reversed().thenComparing(naturalOrder()) for the report.
